caveats: **The eight read actions never set a typed result status.** Every such sample line reads `UNDECLARED / UNKNOWN /` regardless of whether the underlying probe succeeded, partially failed, or hit an unsupported leg (e.g. Linux `manufacturer`/`model`/`bios`/`system` all read `unknown` in the sample, and get the same `UNDECLARED` status as a clean Windows read). A consumer must inspect the row content (`unknown` fields, the `drivers` action's `__truncated__` marker), not the status, to tell success from degradation.

**Two legs are partial: `drivers` on macOS, `memory` on Linux and macOS.** `drivers` is not implemented on macOS. No public per-driver/kext enumeration API exists; the descriptor declares it `YUZU_SUPPORT_UNSUPPORTED` (`hardware_plugin.cpp:858`) and the macOS sample shows the house `unknown` row rather than a capture. `memory` is aggregate-only on Linux and macOS. Linux needs `dmidecode` (typically root) for per-DIMM detail and falls back to `/proc/meminfo`'s total when unavailable or unprivileged; the Linux sample (captured as root/euid 0 in a container) still shows the aggregate `total` row, meaning `dmidecode` itself found nothing usable in that environment even with root. macOS has no public per-DIMM API at all and always reports the aggregate. Separately: On macOS there is no public source for `chassis`, `baseboard` or `machine_id` (the hardware UUID from `system` already identifies the machine), yet all four new actions are advertised `planned` on every OS. The per-OS leg PRs move such legs to a typed `unsupported` with a reason; until then a consumer must read `<os>:planned` as "not read", never as "this host has no value". The appended `cpu`/`dimm` columns are likewise always `-`: `socket_designation`, `stepping`, `manufacturer`, `part_number` and `serial` ride on every `cpu`/`dimm` row so downstream schemas are final, but no leg fills them yet.

**A connected-but-empty WMI query now emits an explicit `unknown` row instead of silently emitting nothing** — a deliberate divergence from the plugin's pre-#3404 behavior, made so a consumer can distinguish "the probe ran and found nothing" from an unrelated dispatch failure (`hardware_plugin.cpp:190-205`). Do not revert this to match the old silent-gap behavior.

**Windows `disks.interface` reports the WMI-layer bus (`SCSI`), not the physical bus** — both drives in the Windows sample are NVMe/SATA but report `SCSI`, because `Win32_DiskDrive.InterfaceType` reports the storage stack layer WMI actually asks, not the physical connector. `disk_actions.smart` decodes the true bus (`nvme`/`sata`/`usb`) via a lower-level IOCTL and is the more accurate source when that distinction matters.

**`drivers_inventory` on Linux derives its signed state from one flag, and only toward "unsigned".** `/sys/module/<module>/taint` holds the module's taint letters; `E` (an unsigned module was loaded) maps to `unsigned`. A module without `E` reads `-`, never `signed`: the kernel may not enforce signatures at all, so the absence of the flag proves nothing. Signer, INF name, hardware id and date have no Linux source and are always `-`; provider and class are the fixed literals `kernel` and `module`, as in `drivers`. A built-in module has no `version` file and reads `-`. A module unloaded between the `/proc/modules` read and its `/sys/module` read also reads `-` (a normal race, not recorded as a failure); a refused or failed `/sys` read is recorded as a status token. Windows: Hitting the cap sets `windows:drivers_inventory:row_cap` and a `constrained` status (the rows read are still emitted). Many `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` rows carry only a hardware id (a device with no driver bound, for example `ACP HDA Node` on the capture host): every other field of those rows is `-`. `DriverDate` is accepted only as a CIM datetime or an ISO date; the locale-formatted text a PowerShell session prints (`21/06/2006 01:00:00`) cannot be read unambiguously and gives `-`. The row escaper folds a backslash to `/`, so a hardware id is written `ACPI/VEN_PNP&DEV_0C0C`. The Windows leg is verified here only by reading and by the pure header's tests; the WMI call itself runs on a Windows host.

definitions.description: Reports the baseboard (motherboard) vendor, product and serial number. Not read yet on any OS: every dispatch answers one unsupported status row (windows:planned, linux:planned or macos:planned) until its leg lands. macOS has no public source and will move to a typed unsupported. It is dispatched by the daily device-record sync: its status, the planned one included, is recorded as the baseboard section, and the baseboard columns of the record fill once the leg reads them.
Returns BIOS or UEFI firmware details: vendor, version, and release date. Uses Win32_BIOS on Windows, /sys/class/dmi/id/bios_* on Linux, and system_profiler Boot ROM on macOS.

Reports the chassis type, serial number and asset tag. Not read yet on any OS: every dispatch answers one unsupported status row (windows:planned, linux:planned or macos:planned) until its leg lands. macOS has no public source and will move to a typed unsupported. It is dispatched by the daily device-record sync: its status, the planned one included, is recorded as the chassis section, and the chassis columns of the record fill once the leg reads them.

Lists physical disk drives with model name, capacity in GB, media type (SSD/HDD/Removable), and interface type (SCSI, NVMe, SATA, USB). Uses Win32_DiskDrive on Windows, native /sys/block on Linux, system_profiler on macOS.

Lists installed device drivers with name, version, date, provider, and device class. Uses Win32_PnPSignedDriver on Windows (the canonical signed-driver registry; the query can take several seconds) and a direct read of /proc/modules on Linux (module names only — version/date are not available without a per-module walk). Not supported on macOS (no public per-driver/kext enumeration API). Supports fleet queries like "devices running driver X older than version Y".

Lists installed drivers in a stable order (sorted by name, INF, hardware id, version; exact duplicates removed) with version, date, provider, device class, signer, signed state, INF name and hardware id. Always leads with one status row: supported when the read was complete, constrained with reason tokens when it was cut short (a row cap of 4096, a refused or failed read), unsupported on macOS. A value that could not be read is "-", never a guess. Windows reads Win32_PnPSignedDriver (bounded WMI, 4096 rows); a device with no driver bound shows only its hardware id. Linux reads /proc/modules plus /sys/module/<module>/version and taint with bounded no-follow reads: the signed state is "unsigned" only when the module's taint flags contain E, and "-" otherwise (no flag proves a module signed); signer, INF, hardware id and date have no Linux source. Not supported on macOS (no public kext/dext enumeration API). The existing "drivers" instruction is unchanged. This is an on-demand question; it is not part of the daily sync.

Reports a keyed hash of the operating system machine identifier. The raw identifier never leaves the host. Not read yet on any OS: every dispatch answers one unsupported status row (windows:planned, linux:planned or macos:planned) until its leg lands; macOS has no source beyond the hardware UUID that device.hardware.system reports and will move to a typed unsupported. It is dispatched by the daily device-record sync: its status, the planned one included, is recorded as the machine id section, and the hashed machine id column of the record fills once the leg reads it.
Returns the system manufacturer string (e.g. "Dell Inc.", "Apple Inc.", "Lenovo"). Uses Win32_ComputerSystem on Windows, /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor on Linux, sysctlbyname(3) on macOS.

Lists installed memory DIMMs with slot locator, capacity in MB, memory type (DDR3/DDR4/DDR5), and speed in MHz. Uses Win32_PhysicalMemory on Windows, dmidecode on Linux (falls back to /proc/meminfo total), sysctlbyname(3) hw.memsize on macOS.
Returns the system model or product name (e.g. "OptiPlex 7090", "MacBookPro18,1"). Uses Win32_ComputerSystem on Windows, /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name on Linux, sysctlbyname(3) hw.model on macOS.

Lists installed CPUs with model name, physical core count, logical thread count, and clock speed in MHz. Uses Win32_Processor on Windows, /proc/cpuinfo on Linux, sysctlbyname(3) on macOS. Returns one row per physical CPU socket.

Reports swap devices and page files with total and used size in MB. Not read yet on any OS: every dispatch answers one unsupported status row (windows:planned, linux:planned or macos:planned) until its leg lands. It is dispatched by the daily device-record sync: its status, the planned one included, is recorded as the swap section, and its rows land in that section once the leg reads them (used size is not recorded).

Returns the machine's hardware serial number and system (SMBIOS / firmware) UUID — the stable CMDB correlation key (e.g. for ServiceNow reconciliation). Windows reads Win32_BIOS.SerialNumber and Win32_ComputerSystemProduct.UUID via WMI; Linux reads /sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial and product_uuid (0400, via the agent's cap_dac_read_search capability); macOS reads IOPlatformSerialNumber and IOPlatformUUID via native IOKit (IOServiceGetMatchingService + IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty against IOPlatformExpertDevice). An absent value (e.g. a VM with no SMBIOS serial) returns the literal "unknown". This is the building block the device_ci daily-sync source (ADR-0016) collects in-process.

description: Reports hardware inventory: manufacturer, model, BIOS, CPU, memory, disks, drivers, chassis, baseboard, swap, machine id
how_it_works:
Thirteen independent actions, dispatched by action name (`hardware_plugin.cpp` `execute()`). `manufacturer`/`model`/`processors`/`system` are single native calls per OS (WMI, `sysctlbyname`/IOKit, or a `/sys`/`/proc` file read) with no subprocess. `bios` and `disks` need data no native API on macOS exposes, so those two legs shell out through the agent's bounded subprocess runner (`run_bounded_subprocess`, fixed deadline, no shell) to `system_profiler` and parse its output with a pure header-only parser (`hardware_macos_bios.hpp`, `hardware_disks_macos.hpp`). `memory` tries `dmidecode` on Linux (also via the bounded runner) and falls back to `/proc/meminfo`'s aggregate total when `dmidecode` is missing or fails. `drivers` enumerates `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` on Windows or reads `/proc/modules` on Linux; it is not implemented on macOS (no public per-driver/kext enumeration API). `drivers_inventory` is its stable-ordered, bounded sibling (the `drivers` action and its rows are unchanged): it adds signer, signed state, INF name and hardware id, sorts every row by (name, INF, hardware id, version), removes exact duplicates, and always leads with one `status|drivers_inventory|<supported|constrained|unsupported>|<tokens or ->` row followed by `driver_inv|<name>|<version>|<date>|<provider>|<class>|<signer>|<signed>|<inf>|<hwid>` rows, `-` standing in for any value that is absent. Windows runs one bounded WMI query on `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` (nine properties, `WHERE DeviceName IS NOT NULL`, a 4096-row cap rather than the 512-row cap the other actions use). Linux reads `/proc/modules` (bounded to 1 MiB, module names validated to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`) and, under one opened `/sys/module` directory descriptor, `<module>/version` and `<module>/taint` with 256-byte no-follow reads; no subprocess runs and no `.ko` file is opened. Ordering, de-duplication, escaping and the status row are one pure header (`hardware_drivers_inventory.hpp`) shared by both legs. The four newest actions (`chassis`, `baseboard`, `swap`, `machine_id`) read nothing yet: each answers with exactly one `status|<action>|unsupported|<os>:planned` row from the shared planned-leg reporter (`agents/shared/planned_leg.hpp`, called from the dispatch in `hardware_plugin.cpp`), until the per-OS leg PRs land the real reads.

Every action that can find nothing still emits one row carrying the literal `unknown` in place of an unread value (`hardware_plugin.cpp:243`, `:257`, `:342-344` and equivalents) — never a silent zero-row output — so a consumer can tell "the probe ran and found nothing" from "this action produced no output for an unrelated reason." This plugin is deliberately not a live-monitoring feed: every action is a point-in-time read with no polling, no event stream, and (except `drivers` and `drivers_inventory`, whose WMI query can take several seconds) no expectation of taking more than a few milliseconds.

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited rows, one per record via `write_output()`. Scalar actions (`manufacturer`, `model`) emit `key|value`; the rest emit one or more `key|field1|field2|...` rows. A field the underlying probe could not read is the literal string `unknown` rather than an omitted field or an empty row — this applies to every read action's identity/value fields (`manufacturer`, `model`, `bios`, `processors`, `memory`, `disks`, `system`); `processors` rows end in two appended columns (`socket_designation`, `stepping`) and `memory` rows in three (`manufacturer`, `part_number`, `serial`), every one the literal `-` until a leg reads it (a DIMM serial is personal data, classified with the system serial, and is not read in this release). The four planned actions emit one typed status row (`status|<action>|unsupported|<os>:planned`) and nothing else. `drivers` additionally emits `__truncated__` in the name field when the Windows WMI row cap (512, `agents/shared/wmi_bounded.hpp`) is hit (`hardware_plugin.cpp:746-753`).

privileges.grant: `system` reads `/sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial` + `product_uuid` (mode `0400`); the packaged systemd unit grants the agent `CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH` as an ambient capability (bounding set limited to that one capability, `NoNewPrivileges` kept), and the dev install script sets `cap_dac_read_search+eip` on the binary instead (`hardware_plugin.cpp:365-371`). The agent clears its inheritable and ambient sets at start, so an exec'd child such as `dmidecode` does not inherit the capability (the in-process read is deliberate). Without the capability (opt-out, `--no-setcap`, or a manual launch) both fields read back `unknown`. The unit also keeps a root-made copy of the firmware tables under `/var/lib/yuzu-agent/dmi/`; this plugin does not read it. Not yet tested on systemd 239 (RHEL 8). `memory`'s `dmidecode` branch typically needs root and fails EPERM unprivileged, silently falling through to the `/proc/meminfo` total (`hardware_plugin.cpp:506-509`).

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result, plus a daily-sync consumer for eleven of the thirteen actions.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. The `device_ci` daily-sync source (ADR-0016) additionally invokes `manufacturer`, `model`, `system`, `bios`, `processors`, `memory`, `disks`, `chassis`, `baseboard`, `machine_id` and `swap` in-process via `LocalDispatcher` and folds their output into its canonical CI record (`agents/core/src/sync_source_device_ci.hpp`), which the server reconstructs field-for-field (`server/core/src/device_ci_ingestion.cpp`). The four newest actions (`chassis`, `baseboard`, `swap`, `machine_id`) are optional sections of that record: each contributes its own status, the planned one included, and a failure in one never stops the report. `drivers` and `drivers_inventory` are not part of the record (`drivers_inventory` is an on-demand question with no gather block). `content/definitions/hardware.yaml:517-518` documents this for the `system` action specifically.

**Not consumed by** Echo, DEX, or metrics. `manufacturer`/`model`/`bios`/`processors`/`memory`/`disks` gather on a 3600s TTL; `drivers` and `system` on an 86400s TTL (`content/definitions/hardware.yaml`); nothing polls continuously.

**Sensitivity.** `system` rows carry the hardware serial number and SMBIOS/firmware UUID — direct, stable device identifiers; `manufacturer`/`model`/`bios`/`disks` name the specific hardware but not a person; `drivers` and `drivers_inventory` rows name installed driver software (`name`/`provider`, plus `signer`, INF name and hardware id on `drivers_inventory`) — a software inventory by another route. No row carries a username or account name.

**Siblings:** `device_identity` (domain/OU join state, same Wave 3 native-acquisition migration), `disk_actions` (SMART health and volume-to-drive mapping — `hardware.disks` reports the drive inventory, `disk_actions` reports its health and logical mounts).

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("device.hardware.system")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
